note: Rav taught that if the altar was damaged, all offerings slaughtered there are disqualified, adding that there was a verse for this but they had forgotten which. When his disciple Rav Kahana went up to the Land of Israel, he heard Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi, teach in the name of Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, that the source is 'You shall slaughter upon it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings': offerings are slaughtered on account of the altar when it is whole, not when it is damaged. Rav Kahana said: this is the verse that eluded Rav.
why: Rav's rule opens a new topic on the damaged altar; the Gemara goes on to set it against Rabbi Yohanan, who says that even animals not yet slaughtered when the altar was damaged are disqualified.

people.name: Rav
people.about: A Sage who knew the ruling on a damaged altar but had forgotten its source verse.

people.name: Rav Kahana
people.about: Rav's disciple, who finds the missing verse in the Land of Israel.

people.name: Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi
people.about: The Sage whom Rav Kahana heard teaching the verse.

people.name: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei
people.about: The Sage in whose name the verse was taught.

terms.meaning: Unfit to be offered, so the sacrifice does not count.
Two kinds of animal sacrifice: a burnt offering is burned whole on the altar, and most of a peace offering is eaten by its owners.
